label: to review
Proposed: Franken
research: Dochnahl, p. 91, calls the party to the Wolfsberg castle-fief agreement Michael von Rosenberg, Schultheiß zu Oggersheim. The same office and town identify him with high confidence as the Michael Rosenberger of 1499-10-04.json and 1507-06-24.json, the husband of Margaretha Dentz. The 1497 settlement (1497-03-21.json) names his father as Michael von Rosenberg. The father’s identification with the Boxberg noble remains probable, supported by the dealings of the same elector with Michael and his Bauland holdings in 1482-01-13.json and 1490-10-28.json. This supports a Franken proposal. The office and marriage evidence give a stronger identification than the surname shared with the Augsburg Rosenegg family. The chronicle’s parenthetical reference to 1545 points to the later Wolfsberg entry (1545_9.json), which concerns a fief at Haardt and does not establish that the two Michaels were the same person or father and son.

entries.source: Dochnahl, Chronik von Neustadt an der Haardt, p. 91
entries.german: Kurfürst Ludwig V. vereinigt sich mit Michael von Rosenberg, pfälzischem Schultheiß zu Oggersheim, wegen eines anderen Burglehens zu Wolfsberg, welches früher der Zollschreiber zu Oggersheim im Genusse hatte. (1545.)
entries.english: Elector Ludwig V reaches an agreement with Michael von Rosenberg, Palatine Schultheiß at Oggersheim, concerning another castle fief at Wolfsberg, formerly enjoyed by the customs clerk at Oggersheim. (1545.)

facts.content: reached an agreement with Ludwig, Kurfürst von der Pfalz, concerning a castle fief at the Wolfsburg previously held by the customs clerk at Oggersheim.
